real_value_base: End-2026 prices (1 Jan 2027). A payment at the start of year Y is deflated over (Y - 2027) years.

us.reason_central: J.P. Morgan 2027 LTCMA US inflation 2.40%, the same edition as the register's 7.5% equity return; it sits between SPF and CBO (2.3%) and the Cleveland Fed model (2.7%), and near the realised 30-year rate (2.56%).
us.reason_low: About the lowest 16-year stretch since 1960 (1.94%, May 2004 to May 2020), the lowest SPF forecaster (1.91%) and the IMF's 2029-2031 path (1.9%).
us.reason_high: The last 10 years ran 3.38%; 3.5% is a little above that and above every 16-year stretch starting since 1984 (max 3.23%); a 1970s repeat (7%) is kept as a stress outside the band.

taiwan_cpi.reason_central: Taiwan's central bank forecasts 1.83% for 2027 and DGBAS 1.90%; the IMF has 1.5-1.8% for 2027-2031; above the 1.2% since 2000 because the last five years ran 2.25%.
taiwan_cpi.reason_low: The lowest 16-year stretch since 1981 averaged 0.98% (1999-2015) and 2000-2020 averaged 0.90%.
taiwan_cpi.reason_high: Above every 16-year stretch since 1981 (max 2.36%, 1981-1997) and the last five years (2.25%); 2022, the worst recent year, was 2.95%.

taiwan_construction.index: DGBAS construction cost index (營造工程物價指數), 2021=100
taiwan_construction.horizon: 2026-2033 (the facility is paid in Jan 2033); the same band is reasonable to 2042
taiwan_construction.reason_central: The index rose 3.0-3.2% a year since 2000 (yearly 2000-2025 3.02%; Sep 2000 to Sep 2026 3.19%); the middle 6-year stretch since 1991 was 3.01% and the middle 16-year 2.88%.
taiwan_construction.reason_low: About the lowest 16-year pace on record (1.60%, 2008-2024); 2010-2020 averaged 1.0% after the 2008 spike.
taiwan_construction.reason_high: Above 9 in 10 six-year stretches since 1991 (4.56%) and the last 10 years (3.91%); lets the current 7.3% pace (wages +9.3%) run two or three more years before fading.
